claim: Select a theme with `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme })` and nothing else. Do NOT write `data-theme`, and do NOT drive the app's own theme control.
evidence: Measured against http://localhost:3003/pricing: emulateMedia('light') gives body background rgb(250,249,247), emulateMedia('dark') gives rgb(18,18,17), and `documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme')` stays null in both. docs/DESIGN.md puts the dark values behind `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, so the media path is the whole job. Writing data-theme fights the app's own theme script; a single click on the theme control only OPENS a dropdown, which is how a half-dark frame came to be reported as a product defect three times in one run.
invalidatesWhen: docs/DESIGN.md stops guaranteeing the media-query path, or `applyTheme` in e2e/helpers/shoot.ts changes

claim: Resolve the dev server with `scripts/ultrabuild/resolve-port.sh` (add `--start` if you are allowed to start one). Never probe the pool by hand, never assume 3000, never kill a server you did not start.
evidence: The rule used to be prose in four prompts and produced 23 port findings across ten rounds. Sixteen concurrent `pnpm dev` servers once put this machine at load average 563 with 4.4 GB of swap, and round 4's gate returned 64 failures of which none was a pixel difference. The script probes /api/dev/seed, which is this repo's own endpoint, so a match proves the server is ours rather than merely alive.
invalidatesWhen: the pool bounds change, or /api/dev/seed stops answering on a dev build

claim: Take blind-pair frames with `scripts/ultrabuild/capture.mjs`. It owns the viewport, the theme, animation suppression, the map-ready wait, the filename and the console classification.
evidence: The procedure used to be ~2 KB of prose that each capture agent re-derived. Cost across two runs: 5 findings about a wrongly switched theme, frames shot with the screen at rest when a hover state was under judgement, flat-colour frames from a WebGL canvas photographed before its first idle, and 36 findings about scratch PNGs left at the repo root.
invalidatesWhen: the script stops covering a state the item needs — extend the script, do not go around it

claim: Our authenticated screens are photographed with Playwright, which holds the demo session in e2e/.auth/demo.json. Ego Lite cannot reach them. A stale session does not fail, it redirects to /login — refresh it with `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port> pnpm exec playwright test --project=setup`.
evidence: Measured: an Ego tab opening /atlas lands on /login?redirect=%2Fatlas, and signing in from inside the task space did not work (no input[type=email], pageInfo() timed out, tab ended on about:blank). Measured again during this review: a cached demo.json against a freshly started server on 3003 redirected /atlas to /login, so the guard in capture.mjs refuses to file that frame.
measuredIn: atlas-tooltips run, rounds 9-12 and post-round-12 review
invalidatesWhen: someone demonstrates Ego Lite carrying our session, with a measurement

claim: A page with a MapLibre canvas is ready when at least one `[data-map-ready]` marker exists AND no `[data-map-ready="false"]` remains. Wait again after every resize and every theme change.
evidence: `settleMap()` in e2e/helpers/shoot.ts makes the same two-sided check, for the same reason: a bare wait on `[data-map-ready="true"]` hangs, because the marker sits on a wrapper Playwright does not always call visible. A theme change replaces the whole style document through setStyle and the marker goes back to false.
invalidatesWhen: src/components/map/map-canvas.tsx stops publishing the marker

claim: A Playwright or vitest failure whose message is a TIMEOUT, with no pixel count and no assertion diff, is evidence about this machine's load and not about the code. Report it; never change code in response to one.
evidence: src/lib/map/__tests__/countries.test.ts timing out at 5000ms is the standing example: it passes 74/74 when run alone. 12 findings in the current run and 10 in the previous one were timeouts of this shape.
invalidatesWhen: a timeout reproduces on an idle machine

claim: A console message whose own stack frame is a Vite dev-server namespace (/@vite/, /@react-refresh, /@id/, /@fs/) is the toolchain talking, not the application. It is not a defect of the item under judgement.
evidence: `ReferenceError: document is not defined` from http://localhost:3001/@vite/client:976 (handleMessage) failed atlas-country-actions and atlas-country-card in round 9. Both were otherwise finished. The gate itself never sees it, because the gate runs no dev client — see TOLERATED_CONSOLE_WARNINGS in e2e/helpers/shoot.ts, which must stay as strict as it is.
invalidatesWhen: the message originates from our own bundle rather than from a dev-server namespace

claim: `pnpm check` (prettier) fails repo-wide on ~157 pre-existing files and is deliberately not part of the mechanical gate. Keep the files you touch prettier-clean; never reformat the repo as a side effect.
evidence: Standing decision, carried in the /ultrabuild command since the first run.
invalidatesWhen: someone formats the repo as its own task

claim: Every screenshot belongs under .claude/ultrabuild/shots/<slug>/round-<n>/<item-id>/, every scratch script in the session scratchpad. Delete what you created once it has served its purpose.
evidence: One run left eleven loose PNGs and two probe scripts at the repo root and a `git add -A` committed 770 KB of them. 36 findings in the current run and 17 in the previous one were about stray artefacts. A root-level PNG/mjs rule in .gitignore is the backstop, not the fix.
invalidatesWhen: never — this is a convention, not a measurement

claim: `extraHTTPHeaders` in playwright.config.ts applies the x-pt-server-today clock pin to EVERY request the context makes, including cross-origin Google Fonts, which rejects the preflight. Every baseline in e2e/__screenshots__ is therefore recorded in the fallback face. Scope the header to the app origin.
evidence: Reported by the auditor of atlas-country-actions: 'Request header field x-pt-server-today is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers'. scripts/ultrabuild/capture.mjs scopes it per-request for exactly this reason.
invalidatesWhen: playwright.config.ts scopes the header, which is open backlog work

claim: The blind critic judges the whole SCREEN, not the component the item owns. Screen-level defects — the 360px composition, a panel's information architecture, a card clipped by its scroll container — will surface while an item that owns none of those files is under judgement.
evidence: In the atlas run, atlas-country-card was repeatedly rejected for defects belonging to src/routes/_app/-ui/atlas-screen.tsx, which it does not own. A component item can only reach acceptance once the screen hosting it is finished, so order the items that way and put the screen-level acceptance on the item that owns the screen.
invalidatesWhen: the capture starts cropping to the item's own element, which it does not

claim: For an item whose point is an interaction state, the capture must photograph THAT state. Declare it in the item's captureStates so scripts/ultrabuild/capture.mjs reaches it; a resting-screen frame is not evidence about such an item.
evidence: Every blind pair in rounds 1-5 of the atlas run photographed /atlas at rest. The critic accepted atlas-map-overlay at high confidence without ever seeing the hover tooltip, which was the entire thing the user had asked for.
invalidatesWhen: never — it is a property of judging by pictures

claim: The translatable surface is ~1,415 unique candidate strings across 263 .ts/.tsx files under src/routes and src/components. It is heavily concentrated: src/routes/_app 680, src/components/modules 316, src/routes/api 267, src/routes/(auth) 146, src/components/marketing 82, src/components/atlas 79, src/components/costs 68, src/routes/legal 65, src/components/layout 45, src/components/ui 28, src/components/map 22, src/components/planner 9.
evidence: Measured before round 1 by scanning JSX text nodes plus copy-bearing props (title|label|hint|description|placeholder|aria-label|message|heading|subtitle|cta|empty|error) over both trees, excluding __tests__. The src/routes/api figure is mostly server JSON and error text rather than screen copy — do not assume all 267 are user-facing. It is an upper bound, not a key count.

claim: Notifications are ALREADY key-based: src/server/repos/notifications.ts stores titleKey + bodyKey + a params JSON record, deliberately never a rendered sentence. Those keys must be rendered through the new catalogue, not re-authored as literals.
evidence: Measured: notifyInput in src/server/repos/notifications.ts validates titleKey and bodyKey as shortTextSchema.min(1) with a params jsonRecordSchema, and the module docstring states the reason — 'a notification written a year ago still renders in the reader's current language'. The rendering sites are src/routes/_app/notifications.tsx and src/components/layout/notification-bell.tsx.
invalidatesWhen: the notifications repo stops storing keys

claim: The reference ships 23 locale directories and 45 namespace files per locale under shared/src/i18n. Its codes are ar br ca cs de en es fr gr hu id it ja ko nl pl ru sv tr uk vi zh zh-TW, where br and gr are its non-standard tags for Brazilian Portuguese and Greek. The 23 chips in the user's screenshot map one-to-one onto that set.
evidence: Measured with the GitHub tree API (repos/liketrek/TREK/git/trees/main?recursive=1) — a directory listing only. The catalogue CONTENTS are AGPL source and docs/SPEC.md §1 and §8.9 forbid reading them into our copy. The canonical tags we ship are fixed in docs/SPEC.md §8; do not re-derive the set from the reference.
invalidatesWhen: docs/SPEC.md §8 changes the shipped set

claim: In the vitest `ui` (jsdom) project, `import.meta.url` is an http: URL, so `fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url))` throws 'The URL must be of scheme file' and fails the whole suite file with 0 failed tests reported. Resolve paths from `process.cwd()` instead — vitest sets it to the project root.
evidence: src/lib/i18n/__tests__/source-rules.test.ts failed with exactly that message while numFailedTests was 0 and numFailedTestSuites was 1; switching to join(process.cwd(),'src','lib','i18n') made it pass. Note the JSON reporter hides this: a suite-level failure shows up only in numFailedTestSuites.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain or the shipped font set changes

claim: The explicit `Record<Locale, () => import('./messages/<tag>')>` loader genuinely code-splits: an SSR `vite build` over src/lib/i18n/catalogue.ts emits exactly 23 separate chunks, one per locale, and none of them is inlined into the entry.
evidence: Scratch config with build.ssr:true and rollupOptions.input=src/lib/i18n/catalogue.ts produced probe-dist/assets containing ar-*.js … zh-Hant-*.js, count = 23, plus catalogue.js. Probe deleted afterwards.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain or the shipped font set changes

claim: `vi.doMock` accepts a path built at runtime (`vi.doMock(`../messages/${tag}`, factory)`), resolves it against the test file, and matches the loader's own `import('./messages/<tag>')` — which is how loader laziness can be measured rather than asserted.
evidence: src/lib/i18n/__tests__/catalogue.test.ts mocks all 23 catalogues in a loop with recording factories; after `await loadCatalogue('pl')` the recorder holds exactly ['pl'], and after 'ar' exactly ['pl','ar']. Requires vi.resetModules() before importing ../catalogue and vi.doUnmock in afterEach.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain or the shipped font set changes

claim: The dev server in the pool can serve a stale CSS transform indefinitely: port 3005 kept returning the pre-edit `styles.css` (old `@import`, old `--font-ui`) after both style files were edited and then `touch`ed, so any CSS change has to be verified by injecting the built stylesheet rather than by reloading the page.
evidence: `curl http://localhost:3005/src/styles/styles.css | grep -c 'Planned Latin Fallback'` returned 0 both before and 3 s after `touch src/styles/tokens.css src/styles/styles.css`, while `dist/client/assets/styles-*.css` from a fresh `pnpm build` contained the rule. In-page `getComputedStyle(document.body).fontFamily` showed the pre-edit stack. Appending `dist/client/assets/styles-*.css` as a `<style>` (it is unlayered-equal and later in source order, so it wins) made the computed stack correct and let the real faces load.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain or the shipped font set changes

claim: `@theme inline` emits `var()` references rather than resolved values, so redeclaring a type token under `:lang()` retunes every Tailwind utility live — but `font-family` inherits as an already-resolved list, so a `:lang()` change to `--font-ui` reaches a whole page and NOT an element that merely carries its own `lang`.
evidence: Built CSS: `.text-title{…line-height:var(--tw-leading,var(--text-title--line-height));letter-spacing:var(--tw-tracking,var(--text-title--letter-spacing))}`. Measured: `<html lang="ar">` moved a `.text-title` from `-0.572px`/`29.9px` to `normal`/`34.32px`. Measured the failure too: a `<button lang="ja">` inside an `lang="en"` page did not use `Noto Sans JP` (absent from `document.fonts` loaded list) until a `:where([lang]:lang(ja)){font-family:var(--font-ui)}` rule was added to re-resolve it; `:where()` keeps specificity at 0 so `.font-display` still wins.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain or the shipped font set changes

claim: Script coverage and metrics of the shipped faces, read from the font binaries — Geist has no Greek, MuseoModerno has neither Greek nor Cyrillic, and only Noto Sans KR of the four CJK faces carries Hangul.
evidence: cmap probe of the Google-served TTFs: geist latin/cyrillic/vietnamese yes, greek no; museomoderno latin/vietnamese only; notosans latin+cyrillic+greek; notosc/tc/jp all carry greek+cyrillic+kana+han but NOT U+D55C, notokr carries it. Metrics (upm 1000, hhea asc/desc/gap, x-height): Geist 1.005/-0.295/0 0.530 · Noto Sans 1.069/-0.293/0 0.536 · Noto Sans Arabic 1.374/-0.738/0 · Noto Sans SC=TC=JP=KR 1.160/-0.288/0 0.543 · Arial 0.905/-0.212/0.033 0.5186. Consequence: the Han faces must sit AFTER Noto Sans in a stack or they claim Greek and Cyrillic.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain or the shipped font set changes

claim: A dev server is OURS only if it answers /api/dev/seed AND its listening process's cwd equals this repo root. A git worktree under .claude/worktrees/ is the same app on a different branch: it answers the same endpoint and is invisible over HTTP. Always resolve with scripts/ultrabuild/resolve-port.sh, which now checks both.
evidence: Measured in round 1. Ports 3002-3005 and 3010 all ran from .claude/worktrees/camping-spots-scraping-plan-79bc83; 3005 and 3010 answered '"ok"' on /api/dev/seed, so the old one-sided probe picked 3005. The entire round-1 gate photographed that sibling checkout and filed 44 visual failures — pricing 4600->4883px, legal-terms 4097->4173px, an atlas country panel that 'never opens', a null chrome.shelf — against code that was never rendered. A hand check of 'does this reproduce on main?' hit the same wrong server and appeared to confirm it. Re-run against a server started from this tree on 3007: 132 passed, 5 skipped, 0 unexpected.
invalidatesWhen: never — an HTTP answer cannot distinguish two checkouts of one app

claim: The x-pt-server-today clock pin is sent to fonts.gstatic.com too, and every woff2 file fails with net::ERR_FAILED, so a pinned context renders in the fallback face while an unpinned one renders in Geist and MuseoModerno. The CSS at fonts.googleapis.com still returns 200, so the failure is silent.
evidence: Measured directly with a Playwright probe on /pricing: clockPin=true gave 'gfonts fail: .../geist/v5/...woff2 :: net::ERR_FAILED | .../museomoderno/v29/...woff2 :: net::ERR_FAILED' and zero real faces loaded; clockPin=false loaded Geist 400/500/600/700 and MuseoModerno 700/800. NOTE: this probe ran against the sibling-worktree server on 3005, so its HEIGHT numbers say nothing about this tree — the CORS mechanism is what it establishes, and it matches the standing clock-pin-cors fact.
invalidatesWhen: playwright.config.ts scopes extraHTTPHeaders to the app origin, which is open backlog work

claim: A missing t() key produces two DIFFERENT TypeScript errors depending on argument count, and the low-information one can be mistaken for the key check being absent. With matching arity you get the clear TS2345 naming MessageKey; with mismatched arity the constraint failure is masked by TS2554 'Expected N arguments'. Check the criterion with a params object present.
evidence: Probe file in src/lib/i18n: `t('language.nope')` -> "error TS2554: Expected 2 arguments, but got 1." (TKey falls back to the MessageKey constraint, whose union of messages requires a params bag). `t('language.nope', { name: 'x' })` -> "error TS2345: Argument of type '\"language.nope\"' is not assignable to parameter of type 'MessageKey'." Both are errors, so the criterion holds, but only the second one says why.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain, the font set or the catalogue layout changes

claim: This checkout is shared with parallel items mid-round, so `git status --porcelain` at the repo root does NOT equal your changedPaths. Scope it to your owned path. src/styles/styles.css and src/styles/tokens.css were dirtied by another agent during my session even though the session-start snapshot said clean.
evidence: `git status --porcelain` listed 7 modified files; `git status --porcelain src/lib/i18n/` listed exactly my 5. The two extra were src/styles/styles.css (+57/-5) and src/styles/tokens.css (+9/-4), whose diff is a new `@layer components` wrapper around the `:where([lang]:lang(ja), [lang]:lang(ko), [lang]:lang(zh-Hant))` font rule — the font/script item, not this one.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain, the font set or the catalogue layout changes

claim: The `:lang()` font re-order rule must live in `@layer components`, not `@layer base`: Tailwind preflight puts `button, input, select, textarea { font: inherit }` in `base` at specificity (0,0,1), which beats a zero-specificity `:where()` in the same layer and hands a `<button lang="ja">` the English stack back. `components` sits after base (preflight loses) and before utilities (`.font-display`/`.font-mono` win).
evidence: Compiled src/styles/styles.css with the installed tailwindcss 4.3.3 `compile()` API and measured getComputedStyle in Chromium on `<button lang="ja">`. Unlayered: .font-display and .font-mono both → 'Geist, Geist Sans, …' (the bug). @layer base: no-utility button → SC-first default stack (preflight regression). @layer components: .font-display → 'MuseoModerno, Noto Sans, Noto Sans Arabic, Noto Sans JP…', .font-mono → 'ui-monospace…', bare lang="ja" → JP-first, lang="ko" → KR-first.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain, the font set or the catalogue layout changes

claim: The metric-compensated `Planned * Fallback` faces make the fallback→webfont swap geometrically free: identical markup measured with only the local() fallbacks and then with all 20 web faces loaded gives byte-identical boxes. And with the 8-family stylesheet wired, all ten scripts share one row height and one baseline.
evidence: Playwright chromium, built dist/client/assets/styles-*.css. Fallback-only (3 faces loaded) vs web-font (20 faces loaded): chips both `[[46.8,24] ×7]`, ja paragraph 46.5px both. CDP CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode over a ten-chip row: en/ru/vi/cs→Geist, el→Noto Sans, ar→Noto Sans Arabic, ja→Noto Sans JP, ko→Noto Sans KR, zh-Hans→Noto Sans SC, zh-Hant→Noto Sans TC; every box 46.8@24. Zero gstatic/googleapis request failures in an unpinned context.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain, the font set or the catalogue layout changes

claim: `--font-han` ordering alone CANNOT route Korean to Noto Sans KR. Noto Sans SC and TC each claim a handful of Hangul syllables in their served unicode-range, and 한, 국 and 어 are all among them — so with SC first, short Korean strings render in SC. Only the `lang="ko"` attribute (via the `:lang(ko)` re-order plus the layered `:where([lang]…)` rule) reaches Noto Sans KR.
evidence: Counted U+AC00–U+D7A3 codepoints across the unicode-range of the served stylesheet: Noto Sans KR 11172, Noto Sans SC 80, Noto Sans TC 49. A per-codepoint probe put 한/국/어 in all three. CDP platform-font check confirms `<button lang="ko">` renders in Noto Sans KR while the same text without `lang` would take SC.
invalidatesWhen: the toolchain, the font set or the catalogue layout changes

claim: The dev server dies with exit code 144 after a while unless the Vite watcher excludes `.claude/**`. `.claude/worktrees/` holds full git worktrees inside the repo root, so chokidar walks another checkout's node_modules and Playwright reports and turns every file its test runs write into a page reload for us.
evidence: Measured: `.claude/worktrees` is 3.2 GB across 95,520 files. The dying server's log was a stream of `[vite] (client) page reload .claude/worktrees/camping-spots-scraping-plan-79bc83/playwright-report/trace/*.html`. vite.config.ts now sets server.watch.ignored to ['**/.claude/**','**/playwright-report/**','**/test-results/**']; after the fix the log contains zero 'worktrees' lines and the server is stable.
invalidatesWhen: the worktrees move out of the repo root, or vite.config.ts loses the ignore list

claim: The i18n parity suite is red BY CONSTRUCTION until the six translation items land, and that redness is not a defect of any English-side item. `src/lib/i18n/messages/en/ui.ts` exists and no `messages/<tag>/` directory does, so the parity test reports every key of every shipped `en` namespace as missing from the other 22 locales. Every further `en/<namespace>.ts` an item ships makes the count worse until `translations-cjk|germanic|romance|rtl-hellenic|sea|slavic` fill their tags, and those six depend on every English-side item. Do NOT repair it from outside a translation item: SPEC §8 gives `messages/<tag>/` wholly to one translation item, so writing a translation from any other item is an ownership violation. An item whose own work is sound is `accepted-pending-gate` here, not rejected.
evidence: Measured at commit 9ee20d4 on a dev server proven to be this worktree: `pnpm typecheck` clean, `pnpm lint` clean, `pnpm test` = Test Files 1 failed | 102 passed (103), Tests 23 failed | 2667 passed (2690). Every one of the 23 failures is src/lib/i18n/__tests__/parity.test.ts, and every reported missing key is a `ui.*` key.
invalidatesWhen: all six translations-* items have shipped their messages/<tag>/ directories

claim: The workflow already returns each recon entry AS `{hash, result}`, so the persist step must write that value VERBATIM. Wrapping it again produces `{hash, result:{hash, result:{topic,facts,...}}}`, and the next round hands the inner wrapper to the workflow as if it were the reader payload. Nothing errors: the run logs `recon reused for: <key>`, `r.topic` and `r.facts` are simply undefined, and that reader contributes an EMPTY section to the digest every builder, critic and auditor reads. Before trusting a cache entry, assert `result.topic` is a string and `result.facts` is non-empty — a matching hash is not proof the payload survived.
evidence: Measured in round 5: recon/stack.json and recon/reference.json were both double-wrapped, so the digest carried 0 of 36 stack facts (plus 20 risks) and 0 of 33 reference facts. Their inner hashes matched their outer ones, which is why the hash check passed. recon/contract.json and recon/codebase.json, written verbatim, were single-wrapped and intact. Unwrapping restored 69 facts and 26 risks. Rounds 3, 4 and the first round-5 attempt all reused the degraded pair.
invalidatesWhen: the persist step writes the returned recon entry verbatim and validates topic/facts before reuse

claim: tailwind-merge in this repo treats `shadow-<token>` as a shadow COLOUR, not a shadow size, so `cn('shadow-card', 'shadow-none')` keeps both classes and CSS source order decides which box-shadow paints. Never rely on `shadow-none` to cancel a token shadow — compose the class list so the shadow is left off instead.
evidence: A test asserting the disabled+selected chip's className `not.toContain('shadow-card')` failed with both `shadow-card` and `shadow-none` present in the merged list. `grep -n shadow src/lib/cn.ts` returns nothing, so no shadow class group is registered in `extendTailwindMerge` and `card` is not on tailwind-merge's built-in shadow size scale.

claim: A component that no route mounts can still be measured in a real browser without touching any file outside ownership: create a programmatic Vite dev server in the scratchpad (`configFile: false`, `resolve: { tsconfigPaths: true }`, `plugins: [viteReact()]`), `ssrLoadModule()` the component and `src/lib/fonts.ts`, render with `renderToStaticMarkup`, inline `dist/client/assets/styles-*.css` plus the real `FONT_STYLESHEET_HREF`, and drive the resulting file:// page with Playwright.
evidence: Produced heights, baselines, column counts, contrast ratios, per-script platform fonts and hover/focus/active/reduced-motion computed styles for LanguagePicker with zero repo files added. Two gotchas measured: a script living outside the repo cannot resolve `vite`/`@playwright/test`, so symlink the repo's node_modules into the scratchpad first; and `playwright` is not installed — the package is `@playwright/test`. Regexing the font href out of fonts.ts yields the raw template literal (`css2?${FONT_FAMILIES.map(`) and loads zero real faces; importing the module gives the real URL and 28 loaded faces.

claim: With the eight-family stylesheet and per-chip `lang`, all seven scripts share one 44px box and one 26px baseline, and CDP confirms each chip gets its own face — so the fixed `h-11` + `leading-7` construction makes 'zero layout shift after paint' true for the catalogue swap rather than merely likely.
evidence: Playwright chromium, unpinned context, 28 faces loaded, zero gstatic/googleapis request failures. Chip height {44} and strut-measured baseline {26} were single-valued sets across en/el/ru/ar/ja/ko/zh-Hans/zh-Hant/vi/cs/id/pt-BR at 360, 393, 768, 1024, 1440 and 2560 in both light and dark. `CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode`: Geist / Noto Sans / Noto Sans Arabic / Noto Sans JP / Noto Sans KR / Noto Sans SC / Noto Sans TC respectively. Skeleton-minus-loaded height delta was 0.00px in all twelve combinations.

claim: drizzle-kit generate can be run entirely in a sandbox, so a 'this file is generated' claim is checkable without writing to drizzle/ — but the `out` path MUST be repo-relative, because drizzle-kit prefixes it with './'.
evidence: An absolute `out` failed with `ENOENT: open './/private/tmp/.../out/meta/0000_snapshot.json'`. With `out: 'node_modules/.dzprobe'` pre-seeded with `cp -R drizzle/meta` plus the 0000/0001 .sql files, and the schema default temporarily set to 'en', `npx drizzle-kit generate --config <scratch>/drizzle.config.ts --name locale_normalisation` wrote 0002_locale_normalisation.sql byte-identical to lines 1-25 of the shipped drizzle/0002_locale_normalisation.sql (sole diff: the shipped file appends '--> statement-breakpoint' to line 25 to join the hand-written data block). Also generated meta/_journal.json idx 2 and meta/0002_snapshot.json. drizzle/ and src/server/db/schema.ts were both clean in `git status` afterwards.

claim: `wrangler d1 migrations apply … --local --persist-to <dir>` gives a throwaway D1 for a from-empty migration test, so you can prove `pnpm db:migrate:local` semantics without touching the shared .wrangler/state a running dev server owns.
evidence: `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply planned-travel-db --local --persist-to <scratch>/d1state` reported 0000 ✅, 0001 ✅, 0002 ✅ (13 commands for 0002, no error). The resulting DB: `locale` text DEFAULT 'en' NOT NULL, no leftover `__locale_normalisation` table, d1_migrations holds all three rows, PRAGMA foreign_key_check and integrity_check both clean. On the shared local D1, `pnpm db:migrate:local` says 'No migrations to apply!' — 0002 was recorded there at 2026-08-23 08:32:55.

claim: A server that passes resolve-port.sh can still be dead for every authenticated screen: port 3006 answers /api/dev/seed with 200 while `/node_modules/.vite/deps/motion_react.js?v=6f0f8d75` returns 504 'Outdated Optimize Dep', so `src/routes/_app/route.tsx` fails its dynamic import and every `_app` route renders the 'Something went off route' boundary. Four successive full reloads did not recover it.
evidence: Playwright with e2e/.auth/demo.json on /settings/appearance: page.url() stays on /settings/appearance (session is valid) but the first h1/h2 is 'Something went off route' on passes 0-3, and the only >=400 responses are two hits on that deps URL. `ls node_modules/.vite/deps/` no longer contains motion_react.js. claim: `rtl:before:-scale-x-100` genuinely reaches the pseudo-element in Tailwind 4.3.3 and composes with a keyframe `transform` rather than replacing it, which is the only way to reverse a physical gradient plus a translateX sweep at once.
evidence: tailwindcss compile() emits `.rtl\:before\:-scale-x-100:where(:dir(rtl), [dir="rtl"], [dir="rtl"] *)::before { --tw-scale-x: calc(100% * -1); scale: var(--tw-scale-x) var(--tw-scale-y) }` — the standalone `scale` property, not `transform`. Measured in Chromium against the built stylesheet: `getComputedStyle(el, '::before').scale` on a `<Skeleton>` is `none` under `<html dir="ltr">` and `-1 1` under `<html dir="rtl">`.

claim: `LOCALE_FORMATS.ar.intlLocale` is the bare tag `'ar'`, whose CLDR default numbering system is `latn` — so `formatNumber(1234,'ar')` is `1,234`, NOT `١٢٣٤`. Arabic-Indic digits belong to `ar-EG` / `ar-u-nu-arab`, which we do not ship. Percent in `ar` also carries U+200E marks.
evidence: node: `new Intl.NumberFormat('ar').format(1234)` -> "1,234"; percent style -> "42‎%‎". Confirmed in-browser through the harness: the ar frames render `2,500` and `+99` in Latin digits. Contrast `tr` -> "%42" (sign prefixed) and `de` -> "1.234" / "42 %". Practical consequence: a test asserting Arabic-Indic digits from this codebase will always fail, and `fr` grouping uses U+202F with U+00A0 before `%`, so `de` and `tr` are the readable locales to assert against.

claim:
Do not run `scripts/ultrabuild/resolve-port.sh --start` under a short Bash timeout. The script polls for readiness after nohup-ing the server, and a SIGTERM to the script takes the server down with it - so the round loses the very server it just started. With a cold `.vite` cache the first identifying request needs several seconds, which is exactly when the naive timeout fires. Give it a long timeout, or spawn `vite dev --port

` detached and poll separately.
evidence: Measured: after `rm -rf node_modules/.vite`, `--start` was killed at 5m (exit 143). Its log shows VITE ready on port 3000 at 00:07, yet nothing was listening afterwards. Re-spawned detached with nohup + disown: the server survived and answered /api/dev/seed in 4.46s on the first request.
invalidatesWhen: resolve-port.sh stops polling in the foreground

evidence: Before the change, `renderToStaticMarkup()` emitted `` and did not contain 'British pound'. After it, the same markup contains the label, and a Playwright context with javaScriptEnabled:false on /settings reads 'Workspace default — en' and 'GBP — Pound sterling' off the triggers. claim: A src/components/ui-only item CAN be measured in a real browser with no repo file added, via an SSR gallery harness — but the harness MUST mount `Direction.DirectionProvider` or it manufactures a phantom RTL overflow defect.
evidence: Recipe that worked: scratchpad `npx vite build -c cfg.mjs` with build.ssr:true, rollupOptions.input=gallery.tsx, external react/react-dom/react-dom/server/react/jsx-runtime, alias '#'->src; then renderToStaticMarkup, inline `dist/client/assets/styles-*.css`, screenshot the file:// page with Playwright. Yielded --thumb-travel 1rem→-1rem, progress scale none→'-1 1', skeleton ::before scale none→'-1 1', --tab-dir 1→-1, weekday 'Mon'→'الاثنين'. THE GOTCHA: without DirectionProvider, Radix Tabs.Root emits dir="ltr", so `start-1` on the segmented pill anchors to the physical LEFT and the pill lands at L=-293 — document.scrollWidth 1193 vs clientWidth 900. Adding the provider takes it to 900/900. Same for the probe scripts: symlink the repo node_modules in, and the package is '@playwright/test', not 'playwright-core'.

claim: Forcing dir="rtl" on a page whose copy is still English reorders a formatted date — '19 Aug 2026' renders as 'Aug 2026 19'. That is a UAX#9 capture artefact, NOT a product defect, because a real `ar` reader gets Arabic month names from the frozen table.
evidence: Measured on /settings after `document.documentElement.setAttribute('dir','rtl')`: the <dd> textContent is exactly '19 Aug 2026' with computed direction rtl and unicode-bidi isolate, yet it paints 'Aug 2026 19'. UAX#9 N1 treats EN as R, so the space between '19' (EN) and 'Aug' (L) has no matching pair, N2 gives it the RTL embedding level, and the two level-2 runs are then laid out right-to-left against each other. formatDate(..., 'ar') returns '19 مارس 2026', which is native RTL and orders correctly, so the condition that produces this never occurs in the shipped product.

claim: ultrabuild.js:1172 pushes a rejection reason whenever there is no visual verdict AND the item carries `url` or `referenceUrl`. Acceptance text cannot reach that rule - the verdict assembler never reads acceptance - so an item with a url whose reference cannot be photographed is rejected EVERY round no matter how good its work is. For a library item with no screen of its own, the fix is to remove `url`, which is the mechanism the workflow already provides.
evidence: ui-primitives-i18n-rtl was rejected in rounds 5 and 6 with the identical reason 'no blind pair', zero blocking findings against its own work, and abWinner null. language-picker and locale-persistence both reached accepted-pending-gate with no pair either - and neither carries a url. Removing the url from ui-primitives-i18n-rtl is the whole fix.
invalidatesWhen: the verdict assembler learns to read an acceptance criterion that waives the visual lens
